title: The database disk is filling up, and the tables aren't growing
intro: The disk alert on the primary database host fired at 85% and it's now at 94%, climbing about 1% every ten minutes. Table sizes haven't changed. At 100% PostgreSQL will stop with a PANIC and take the shop down. The data directory is /var/lib/postgresql/16/main.

steps.prompt: Find what's using the space inside the data directory: show the size of each of its subdirectories, largest last.
pg_wal holds 371 GB; it's normally a few GB. Something is stopping PostgreSQL from recycling old WAL. First rule out the archiver: check whether WAL archiving is failing.

Archiving is healthy. The other thing that pins WAL is a replication slot. List the slots with whether each is active and how much WAL it's holding back: select slot_name, active, and pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) from pg_replication_slots.
expected_commands: psql -c "SELECT slot_name, active, pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) FROM pg_replication_slots;"
psql -c "SELECT slot_name, active, pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) FROM pg_replication_slots"
steps.fake_output:
slot_name      | active | pg_size_pretty
--------------------+--------+----------------
 pg_2               | t      | 16 MB
 pg_3               | t      | 48 MB
 analytics_cdc_test | f      | 369 GB
steps.hint: SELECT slot_name, active, pg_size_pretty(pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), restart_lsn)) FROM pg_replication_slots;

steps.prompt: A slot named analytics_cdc_test is inactive and holding 369 GB. The analytics team confirms it was a change-data-capture trial that ended two weeks ago. Drop the slot.
Old WAL is removed at the next checkpoint. Don't wait for it: force one now.
Confirm the space came back: check the filesystem holding /var/lib/postgresql.
steps.fake_output:
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/nvme1n1    500G  103G  397G  21% /var/lib/postgresql

steps.prompt: Make it impossible for a forgotten slot to fill the disk again: set max_slot_wal_keep_size to 50GB server-wide.

resolution: A replication slot is a promise: the primary keeps every WAL file the slot's consumer hasn't read yet, so the consumer can disconnect and catch up later. When the consumer never comes back, the promise never expires. Two weeks ago a change-data-capture trial created the slot analytics_cdc_test; the trial ended, the consumer was switched off, and the slot stayed. PostgreSQL then kept two weeks of WAL, 369 GB, until the disk was nearly full. The tables hadn't grown at all, which is the clue: when a database disk fills without the data growing, look at pg_wal, and then at the two things that pin WAL, a failing archive_command and an inactive slot. Dropping the slot and forcing a checkpoint freed the space within seconds. Had the disk reached 100%, PostgreSQL would have shut down, and the fix would have started with finding space just to start it again (never delete files from pg_wal by hand: that corrupts the database). Prevention: max_slot_wal_keep_size puts a ceiling on what any slot may retain, after which the slot is invalidated instead of the disk filling; alert on retained WAL per slot and on any slot with active = false; and treat a slot like any other resource that must be deleted when its consumer is.
